seo.title: Copilot SEO: How to Get Cited by Microsoft Copilot
seo.meta_description: Copilot SEO explained: Copilot answers are grounded in Bing, so get indexed in Bing, use IndexNow, answer directly and track copilot.microsoft.com referrals.

h1: Copilot SEO: How to Get Your Site Cited by Microsoft Copilot
answer: Copilot SEO is about getting your pages cited in Microsoft Copilot's answers. Copilot grounds its web answers in Bing, so the essentials are to get indexed and healthy in Bing Webmaster Tools, notify Bing instantly with IndexNow, allow Bingbot, and publish clear, specific answers that Copilot can quote with a link.
key_takeaways: Copilot's web answers are grounded in Bing search results.
Bing Webmaster Tools is the Search Console of Copilot visibility.
IndexNow tells Bing about new and updated pages immediately.
Copilot reaches buyers inside Windows, Edge and Microsoft 365.
Copilot citations are links, so visits are easy to measure.

sections.heading: Why Copilot belongs in your GEO plan
sections.body_html:
Microsoft Copilot is built into Windows, the Edge browser and Microsoft 365, which puts it in front of a huge number of people at work. Many B2B buyers meet it while researching vendors at their desks. When Copilot answers a question with web information, it shows the sources it used, giving your pages a direct, clickable route to that buyer.

Copilot also shapes decisions that never produce a click. A buyer who reads a Copilot summary naming your company may search for you directly days later, or forward the summary to a colleague. Being named accurately, with your specialty and location right, matters even when the visit comes later through another channel.

sections.heading: How Copilot finds sources
sections.body_html:
Copilot's web answers are grounded in Bing. In simple terms: the question goes to Bing, Bing returns relevant pages from its index, and Copilot summarizes them with citations. That makes Bing visibility the foundation of Copilot visibility. A page Bing has not indexed, or ranks poorly, is unlikely to be cited.

Bing also supplies web results to other products, so this work tends to help beyond Copilot.

sections.heading: The Copilot SEO checklist
sections.body_html:
1. Verify your site in Bing Webmaster Tools and submit your sitemap. You can import your sites from Google Search Console to save time.
  2. Check indexing and errors in Bing's reports, and fix crawl issues it finds.
  3. Turn on IndexNow so Bing hears about every new or updated page the moment it changes.
  4. Allow Bingbot in robots.txt and in any firewall or bot-protection tool.
  5. Answer first on every key page, with descriptive headings and FAQs.
  6. Add structured data that matches the page, and keep titles and descriptions specific.

sections.heading: Content that Copilot cites
sections.body_html:
Copilot users often ask practical work questions: how to do something, which tool to pick, what something costs. Pages that answer those well share a pattern:

  • Plain-language definitions in the first sentence.
  • Numbered steps for processes.
  • Comparison tables for choices between options or vendors.
  • Clear facts with dates, so the answer stays current.
  • Named expertise: who wrote it and why they know.

sections.heading: Bing Webmaster Tools features worth using
sections.body_html:
• URL inspection to see whether a page is indexed and why not.
  • Site scan to find technical SEO issues.
  • Search performance to see the queries and pages Bing shows you for.
  • Sitemaps and IndexNow reports to confirm Bing is receiving your updates.

Check it monthly alongside Google Search Console. Problems often show up in one before the other.

sections.heading: Measuring Copilot traffic
sections.body_html: Clicks from Copilot answers usually arrive with copilot.microsoft.com or a bing.com address as the referrer. Add them to your AI search channel in Google Analytics, track landing pages and leads, and test your top buyer questions in Copilot each month.

sections.heading: Copilot for B2B buyers
sections.body_html:
Because Copilot sits inside the tools people use at work, B2B buyers often meet your brand there first. A procurement manager asks Copilot to compare vendors in Edge; a founder asks it to summarize options in a Word document. For those buyers, create pages that answer evaluation questions directly:

  • "[Your category] for [industry]" pages with specifics for that industry.
  • Comparison pages that explain how your approach differs and when another option fits better.
  • Pricing and process pages that explain how engagements work, what is included and how long they take.
  • Security, compliance and integration details where they matter to buyers.

sections.heading: Copilot SEO vs Google SEO
sections.body_html:
Google SEOCopilot SEO
Index that mattersGoogleBing
Webmaster toolGoogle Search ConsoleBing Webmaster Tools
Fast discoverySitemaps and internal linksSitemaps plus IndexNow
Where buyers see youSearch results and AI OverviewsCopilot answers in Windows, Edge and Microsoft 365

Most of the work overlaps, so doing both rarely doubles the effort. The main extras are verifying in Bing and turning on IndexNow.

sections.heading: How to test your Copilot visibility
sections.body_html:
Testing Copilot works like testing any AI engine, with one Bing-specific twist: compare what Copilot says with what Bing shows for the same question.

  1. Pick 20 buyer questions and ask each in Copilot.
  2. Record mentions and citations, noting which pages are linked.
  3. Search the same questions in Bing and note where your pages rank.
  4. Compare. If you rank well in Bing but are never cited, improve the opening answer and structure of the page. If you do not rank in Bing at all, fix indexing and relevance first.

This comparison quickly shows whether the problem is discovery (Bing) or presentation (the page itself).

sections.heading: Mistakes that hide you from Copilot
sections.body_html:
• Never verifying the site in Bing, so indexing problems go unseen.
  • Blocking Bingbot through a security tool built only with Google in mind.
  • Waiting weeks for Bing to rediscover updated pages instead of using IndexNow.
  • Vague pages that never answer the specific question.

faqs.a: It is the work of getting your pages cited in Microsoft Copilot's answers. Because Copilot grounds web answers in Bing, it focuses on Bing indexing, IndexNow, crawl access for Bingbot and clear, specific pages.
Yes. Copilot's answers that need web information are grounded in Bing search results, which is why Bing indexing and ranking matter for Copilot visibility.
IndexNow is a protocol that lets websites notify participating search engines, including Bing, the moment a page is added or updated, instead of waiting for the next crawl.

faqs.q: Do I need Bing Webmaster Tools if I have Google Search Console?
faqs.a: Yes. Bing has its own index and reports. You can import your sites from Search Console, then use Bing's tools to find indexing problems that affect Copilot.

faqs.q: Can I see traffic from Copilot?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Visits from Copilot citations often show copilot.microsoft.com or bing.com as the referrer in Google Analytics. Group them into an AI search channel.
Often, yes. Copilot is built into Windows, Edge and Microsoft 365, so many professionals use it while researching vendors and tools during the workday.
